questions: Drawing on her own pioneer childhood, this American writer and former teacher penned a beloved children's book series published in the 1930s and early 1940s — who was she?
Laura Ingalls Wilder (February 7, 1867 - February 10, 1957) was an American writer, teacher, and journalist.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Castel Sant'Angelo (founded 139) is the earliest of the four.

Renowned for a gift of mimicry noted by Pliny the Elder and Shakespeare, this glossy black bird has a bill that turns from black in winter to yellow in summer — what species is it?
Common starling: Species of passerine birds.
Animal taxa named by Carl Linnaeus
Which of these four was founded earliest?

AC Milan (founded 1899) is the earliest of the four. In its early history, Milan played its home games in different grounds around the city before moving to its current stadium, the San Siro, in 1926.
Meaning 'The Hope' in Hebrew, this national anthem's lyrics were adapted from an 1877 poem written by Naftali Herz Imber while he was staying in Iași — which anthem?
Hatikvah: National anthem of Israel. Hatikvah (Hebrew: הַתִּקְוָה [hatikˈva]; lit. 'The Hope') is the national anthem of the State of Israel.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Rachel (born 1729 BC) is the earliest of the four.
This Japanese actor, known for his role as Doc in a long-running detective drama, was once married to singer Seiko Matsuda, with whom he had an actress daughter — who is he?
Masaki Kanda (born December 21, 1950) is a Japanese actor.
